## The rule, in one line

A **non-fork** resume of a **tracked** session re-registers under the **original**
`coordOwnerId`. Everything keyed on that id — locks, awaits, presence, an open UI
pane — keeps working. Take away either qualifier and identity does **not** survive.

> Cite these by **symbol name, never line number**. Every line number in this doc's own
> commissioning note had drifted by the time it was written a few hours later
> (`resumeEnvFor` moved ~2580 → 2644). Grep the symbol.

## `resumeEnvFor` is the whole story

`resumeEnvFor(session, { mintSid, fork })` in `apps/operator/scripts/psu-launcher.mjs`
is pure and exported for tests, which is what makes this cheaply checkable — you can
read the branch instead of running a resume and inferring.

The non-fork branch returns:

```js
return {
  PAPERCUSP_AGENT: session.agent,
  PAPERCUSP_SID: session.coordOwnerId || mintSid(),
  ...(session.workspaceId ? { PAPERCUSP_WORKSPACE: session.workspaceId } : {}),
  ...(session.id != null ? { PAPERCUSP_ADV_SESSION_ID: String(session.id) } : {}),
};
```

Three things ride on that, and each has its own failure mode:

- **`PAPERCUSP_SID: session.coordOwnerId`** — wake-executor semantics. The old behaviour
  (a fresh random SID per resume) orphaned the original SID's locks/awaits/presence and
  detached the live session from its adv row *mid-stream*.
- **`PAPERCUSP_WORKSPACE`** — without it a resumed session loses workspace scoping and
  every workspace-scoped tool fails with `no workspace transaction`. This is not a
  nice-to-have; it is the difference between a working session and a dead one.
- **`PAPERCUSP_ADV_SESSION_ID`** — the link back to the adv row.

## The trap: an untracked row mints a fresh SID

`session.coordOwnerId || mintSid()` — the `||` is the trap. An **untracked** session has
no adv row, therefore no `coordOwnerId`, therefore it falls through to a **freshly
minted** SID and gets no workspace either. The operator's SID→adv-row fallback cannot
help those, because there is no row to fall back to.

Nothing errors. The resume succeeds. But anything still holding the OLD id — a UI keyed
on it, a lock, a peer's `events:await`, a queued wake — now points at an id **that will
never exist**. The failure surfaces later, somewhere else, as "the agent never
responded".

## `fork: true` inverts the rule on purpose

The fork branch always mints a fresh SID and sets **no** adv-row link. That is not an
oversight to be "fixed" — a fork is a genuinely new session, not a second body of the
original, and the fresh identity is exactly what lets it run **concurrently with the
still-live original** without colliding on its locks, presence, or inbox-wake. Workspace
scope still carries over (a fork stays in the same workspace).

So `fork` is the switch between *"come back as the same agent"* and *"start a sibling"*.
Sending it on a path that means the first is a silent identity split.

## The generalisable lesson: gate the render on the predicate identity depends on

This is the part worth carrying to other features.

The "Resume in GUI" button (`AgentInspectorModal.tsx`) opens a conversation with a
resumed agent. It is correct **only because its render gate and the identity guarantee
share one predicate**: it is gated on `guiOwnerId`, whose inactive-session source *is*
`session.coordOwnerId` — the very field whose absence is what breaks identity. So the
button hides in exactly the case where resuming would not preserve the id. It is aligned
**by construction, not by luck**:

```jsx
{resumeTarget?.canFork && resumeTarget.guiOwnerId && onOpenInGui ? ( … ) : null}
```

**Two edits silently reintroduce a dead popup — do not make either:**

1. **Loosening the gate** to fall back to some other id when `coordOwnerId` is null. The
   button then renders for untracked sessions and opens a pane keyed on an id the
   resumed session will never register under.
2. **Sending `fork: true` on the GUI path.** The resume succeeds, a *different* agent
   comes up, and the pane waits forever on the original id.

Both are pinned by tests, and it is worth knowing which test catches which — a change
that defeats one is not caught by the other:

| the edit | the test that fails |
|---|---|
| `fork: true` on the gui path | `POSTs the SAME resume with headless:true (no window, never a fork) and hands the owner id to the host` — asserts the wire body with `toEqual({ …, fork: false, headless: true })` |
| loosening the render gate | `is hidden with no coord owner id to key the conversation on` |

The transferable form: **when a UI affordance depends on an invariant that only holds
under some condition, gate the affordance on that same condition** — not on a proxy for
it, and not on a second id that "usually" agrees. A proxy makes the alignment a
coincidence that the next edit is free to break.

## `--headless` is not cosmetic

The GUI path sends `headless: true`, and that flag is load-bearing.
`packages/operator-core/lib/console-spawn.ts` states the invariant on
`SpawnHeadlessOpts.envelope`: the greeting **MUST** be a `psu --headless …` command
*"for the session to stay injectable"*. That is what makes psu-launcher take the managed
pty host despite non-TTY stdio (`usePtyHost` + `PAPERCUSP_PSU_HEADLESS=1`) — and that pty
is precisely what a `coord:send { wake: 'required' }` injects into. Drop the flag and you
get a session that starts fine and can never be woken.

`spawnHeadless` is not a side path: it is the same `buildConsoleOneliner` output
`spawnConsole` runs, just wired to a log file instead of a terminal window, and it is
production-proven under `capability:launch-agent`, headless `fleet:launch-on-plan`
fleets, fleet-headcount-action, and p2p delegated-spawn. Its log dir is the per-workspace
`.papercusp/fleet-logs`, so **a log there is evidence that a headless spawn actually
happened** — useful when you need to prove a spawn rather than assert it.

## Checking any of this

```bash
grep -n 'export function resumeEnvFor' apps/operator/scripts/psu-launcher.mjs
grep -n 'guiOwnerId' apps/operator/app/harness/AgentInspectorModal.tsx
grep -n 'stay injectable' packages/operator-core/lib/console-spawn.ts
```

`resumeEnvFor` being pure and exported means you never have to run a resume to answer
"would identity survive here?" — read the branch.
